text:
Predicates:
Costs(x, y) ::: x costs y.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
ProvidesAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
ProvesHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
Applies(x, y) ::: x is applying to y.
Premises:
Costs(ge, 205) ∧ Cheaper(ge, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
ProvidesAid(ets, y) ← ProvesHardship(y) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those who prove hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(tom) ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
Applies(tom, gre) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Costs(gre, 205) ∧ Cheaper(gre, 300) ::: It costs below US $300 to take the GRE test.
